title: Come with me if you want big shoulders (JOIN THE CHALLENGE!)
summary: NH launches a one-year community shoulder challenge for 2023 with a flexible master plan: 1-2 vertical presses plus 2-3 lateral isolations, capped rep ranges, 12-20 weekly sets, and progression measured by tonnage and strength at the same reps. He explains his own plan (barbell OHP plus three raise variations, 3x/week), placement within splits, managing horizontal pressing, and novice and intermediate examples.
claims: He de-prioritised shoulders for two years (no vertical pressing) so his biceps and triceps would overpower his delts; now his arms are big enough to let the delts catch up
The challenge uses only time-tested methods and direct work: vertical presses as the bread and butter, plus isolations that spare the elbow and wrist
Progress metric is tonnage, but tonnage must be raised through intensity (more weight for the same reps with the same technique), not by piling easy sets that become junk volume
Do not dirty bulk for the challenge; recomp or gain weight slowly
Pick 1-2 vertical presses and 2-3 shoulder isolations: minimum 3, maximum 5 shoulder movements, to stay specific while varying planes to spare tendons
Pick presses you enjoy and can do comfortably long-term, not 'optimal' ones; the only requirement is that it is a vertical press
For isolations any movement that hits the three delt heads and spares the joints works, even upright rows
Use 1-2 rep ranges per press (max 4 across presses) and one rep range per isolation; too many rep ranges make progression impossible to track
Recommended compound rep ranges: 4-8, 6-10 or 8-12; never below 4 reps, max 12
He no longer goes below 6 reps on the overhead press because lower reps degraded his form and he stopped feeling the shoulders
He tested the plan for three months beforehand: shoulders catching up and perfect tendon health
Isolation rep ranges: 8-12 or 10-15; going above 15 risks junk volume
Per session do 3-4 sets of compounds then 3-4 of isolation; the more shoulder sets per day, the less intense each can be
Weekly vertical press volume: 6-8 sets, can go to 12 or even 16 if you recover fast; vertical presses barely tax him
Weekly isolation volume 6-12 sets; total 12-20 shoulder sets per week
Progression example: build from 12 to 15-16 weekly sets at the same weight, then increase load and drop back to 12 sets
Placement: full body anywhere; push/pull/legs presses on push day and isolations on legs day; upper/lower presses on upper days, isolations anywhere
Spread shoulder sessions to maximise recovery between them
One-half rule: on an N-day split cycle, put shoulder work on about half the days (2 of 3, 2 of 4, 3 of 6), independent of calendar weeks
You only have one set of shoulders, so horizontal pressing volume competes with vertical pressing
In his experience vertical pressing done properly is not taxing on the shoulder and even helps joint health; doing it after horizontal presses tends to work better than before
He presses with a barbell OHP for 6-10 and 8-12, using the 6-10 as an intensity deload
He never locks out the overhead press because it gives him elbow tendinitis; lockout only adds triceps and trap work, so do not let anyone bully you into it
He hates standing lateral raises because they hurt his shoulder; he holds the rack and leans his torso to raise in a comfortable range
Progressing 10-15 lb on lateral raises over a year with strict form at the same rep range will make shoulders bigger
His plan: OHP plus DB lateral raises, cable lateral raises and bent-over raises, 3x/week, targeting 12-16 shoulder sets per week
Most people can do more isolation sets than compound sets because isolations are less fatiguing
Novice example: one vertical press (e.g. OHP 8-12) and one lateral raise (10-12), 3-4 sets each, once a week: 6-8 total sets is all a novice needs
Failure is optional: he stops at 1 RIR on presses because grinding the last rep tweaks his neck and upper back nerve damage, but goes to failure on isolations
Evolving set/rep range: e.g. OHP 4x8-12 at 100 lb; once you hit 12/11/10, add 2.5 lb and drop to 3 sets, then build sets back up
Intermediate example: barbell OHP 3x4-8, DB OHP 4x8-12, upright row 4x10-15, about 11-12 weekly sets
The upright row is not a lift to ego-lift or max out on
Start with the fewest sets possible at high intensity and ramp up to monitor shoulder health
Compounds give more fatigue and more stimulus, so they are the priority; you will not get big round natural shoulders from lateral raises alone; if you must skip, skip an isolation set
exercises: main vertical press; lockout causes elbow tendinitis for him
8-12, hardest part is getting DBs to shoulders
